If you're nostalgic for RoboCop then this game is probably for you. However, you're not playing a AAA game.
The gameplay follows this lifecycle:
1. Drawn out cut-scenes
2. Arcade style shoot outs
Walking
3. Minutae missions
4. Repeat
You can tell shortcuts were taken despite the glossy graphics. Get it while it's cheap and prepare to turn your brain off.

The game is a satiric parody of excessive nationalism.

It's explosive, chaotic, and everything can kill you. But there is little disappointment in death due to the way the game is set up. You can completely finish a mission and fail to extract and still get the mission rewards (Aside from samples and the occasional side objective that requires extracting with an item).

The in-game currency used to purchase warbonds (battlepasses) can be farmed from missions. Although it takes time, it essentially means you can spend $0 and still have access to all the games warbond content.

I recommend on sale.

This IS a good game, but it's not a 10/10. I like the story, the characters, the narrative, the music, the expressive visuals and the length (these types of games are purposefully short). I didn't like the ending, which felt very abrupt and anti-climactic (would've been cool to have a time jump at the end to see what happened to the characters). I also feel that the mini-games could've been more polished and deeper. I understand that they aren't the main focus, but they kind of are an essential part, so they could've been fleshed out to make the player more engaged.

Your enjoyment of this game will heavily depend on your fondness of the following things:
* Walking sims / mini-games
* Slice of life genre
* 80's & 90's nostalgia
* Music history (primarily 70's to 90's)
I reccomend it. Fun game to shoot bad guys.

I will continue to buy everything that Kyle Thompson puts out! As a game developer that tried my hand at small team indie games unsuccessfully, I have an immense respect for Kyle’s mastery of a genre that I love. While the underlying formula is shared across his games, every game has an interesting theme and a unique take somewhere in there. I can feel his love for the craft in every game and it’s utterly impressive.

I found this to be a really charming game. At first, I thought it is one of those cleanup games, and in many ways it is, but there is a narrative and an objective and levels that are more like connected hubs. The game is mechanically simple, zero interface, and it is just you and your partner chatting over comms as you unravel the mysteries of the world. 

At more or less four hours, I think it does not overstay its welcome. Cleaning up the gunk really is satisfying, and I actually did like the banter, character design, and graphics.

Each act out of 3 is very long and all of the different locations are so fun to play and have beautiful design(Except Bilewater from the looks of things XD). The bosses are exceptionally hard but have a very fun pattern once you learn the attacks! I'm currently fighting the final boss of Act 1,The Last Judgewho is extremely difficult for me, but just as good! The sound design is also phenomenal, it's very immersive and I love thebell sound effects. Please give this game a shot, considering you've played Hollow Knight first at least!
